{
  "key": "gh-1140",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[GOAL] Guest fork PRs become machine PRs via po_accept transplant — zero fork CI, zero fork lanes (supersedes #1139)",
    "description": "## Goal — Guest fork PRs become ordinary machine PRs via human-armed transplant (v1)

One sentence: **a third-party fork PR, once a human labels it `po_accept`, is transplanted by the SM into a machine PR of the base repository, passes a mandatory Security Gate phase, and from that point on is indistinguishable from any ordinary machine PR — zero fork-specific lanes, zero permanent guest mode.**

Today a fork PR in a dispatch-only-CI repo can neither run validation (workflow_dispatch rejects fork branch names AND `refs/pull/N/head` — both pinned live 2026-10-20, HTTP 422) nor satisfy required check contexts, so the approved FIFO stalls behind it (live: fah #1591/#1615/#1634 for 20+ hours). This card replaces every fork-special path with one rule: move the code, then behave as if the fork never existed.

## Why this framing

- The #1139 framing (validate on a throwaway merge-result branch, stamp contexts onto the fork head, extend the gh-113 guest merge lane) is **retracted**: it keeps a parallel fork universe (stamp semantics, guest zero-red probes, branch GC) alive forever. The transplant framing deletes the problem instead of managing it — RCA text of #1139 stays valid, its fix direction is superseded.
- gh-113's manual `ai_validating` arm + zero-red merge stays as the pre-existing fallback lane; this card does not modify it.

## Architecture

```
fork PR (guest)          base repo                        base repo
──────────────          ─────────                         ─────────
#NNN + po_accept ──▶ rule guest-transplant:
                        1. branch ai/guest-NNN = API merge(main, headSHA)
                        2. open machine PR "[guest #NNN] <title>"
                        3. close #NNN + comment "transplanted at <sha> → #MMM"
                        4. carry review verdicts iff diff identical
                                       │
                                       ▼
                        standard machine lanes (validate-fresh →
                        merge-validated → merge); NO new merge logic
```

- **Protocol "guest transplant"**: one SM rule `guest-transplant` + one localAction `transplant_guest_pr`. Query: open, non-draft, `po_accept` label, NOT machine-authored, head IS cross-repo. limit 1 per tick (a transplant creates a PR + closes another — serial by construction, same discipline as the merge window).
- **Invariants**:
  - The SM never dispatches CI on any fork-owned ref — impossible-by-construction (no code path targets them).
  - The transplanted PR is machine-authored and enters a **Security Gate phase FIRST**: every security check (code scanning, secret scan, dangerous-diff scan — the Gate manifest is repo-configurable) must conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming job of the transplant's validation runs; the ordering is enforced structurally (workflow job `needs`), not by convention.
  - Once the Gate is green the guest provenance is erased from all routing: the PR flows through validate-fresh → merge-validated exactly like a same-repo machine PR. Guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode.
  - One live transplant per source PR at a time; a second `po_accept` on an already-transplanted source is a no-op with an audit line (snapshot semantics).
- **Fallback paths**: merge API conflict (409) → park the source PR with label `blocked` + a distinct-reason comment naming the conflict (v1); source branch deleted before the tick runs → same park with the no-ref reason; verdict carry impossible (diff drifted) → transplant proceeds WITHOUT carried labels (fresh pipeline).

## Capability surface (everything the platform allows → our shape)

| Platform fact (pinned) | Our shape |
|---|---|
| `workflow_dispatch` rejects fork branch names (422 "No ref found", live fah 2026-10-20) | Never attempted; fork heads are transplanted instead |
| `workflow_dispatch` rejects `refs/pull/N/head` (422, live) | Never attempted |
| Merges API accepts a pull-head SHA as `head` (live: validate/pr-1591 = API merge of f7a8fcbe) | Transplant branch = `POST /merges` base=`ai/guest-NNN` (cut at main) head=source SHA |
| Fork head SHAs are addressable in the base repo (refs/pull/N/head fetchable) | No clone of the fork is ever needed |
| PAT silent-update of fork branches works (SILENT_GH_TOKEN, live fah#1721) | Source branch freshness before transplant: best-effort silent-update, NOT required (merge resolves against current main anyway) |
| API ref create + branch delete are available to the stub token | Branch `ai/guest-NNN` lifecycle owned by the SM; deleted when the transplant PR closes |
| GitHub check-run stamping exists (checks:write) | NOT used for guests — nothing is ever stamped on a fork head |
| Workflow job graph (`needs:`) can order jobs within one run | The Security Gate is a real job-level precondition: secret-consuming validation jobs declare `needs: security-gate` on guest-transplant runs — the ordering cannot be bypassed by the dispatcher |

### Tiered inventory

- **Core (this card)**: the `po_accept` rule; transplant branch + machine PR creation; source close + comment; the Security Gate phase (ordered, mandatory, manifest-configurable) ahead of ordinary validation; conflict/no-ref parks; branch GC; snapshot semantics.
- **Second tier (opt-in follow-ups)**: trusted-contributor allowlist (auto-arm po_accept for named logins, owner-configured); auto-rework leg on transplant conflict (machine resolves, replays transplant); carrying linked-issue wiring (labels on the source issue).
- **Excluded (rationale)**: running ANY CI on fork-owned refs (impossible via dispatch, unwanted via pwn-request surface); transplanting PR comments/conversation history (conversation stays on the closed source, linked by the close comment); auto-arm by review verdict alone (a human must vouch for CODE EXECUTION risk — the label is the voucher).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — labeling an open, cross-repo, non-draft fork PR `po_accept` (by a human, non-machine actor) leads, within one tick, to: branch `ai/guest-NNN` (merge of source head into current main), an open machine PR titled `[guest #NNN] <original title>` with `Co-authored-by:` trailer and a body linking the source, and the source PR closed with a transplant comment naming both SHAs.
- **AC2** — the transplanted PR enters the standard pipeline: validate-fresh dispatches on its branch, merge-validated merges it; no guest-specific merge rule fires anywhere in that chain.
- **AC3** — on a guest-transplant run, every secret-consuming validation job is unreachable while any Security Gate job is non-green (`needs:` wiring asserted by UT on the dispatched job graph; E2E red-gate fixture shows the secret job never started), and after the Gate is green the SAME run's later jobs execute with the full ordinary secret set — guest and non-guest validation runs are structurally identical apart from the Gate prefix.
- **AC4** — a merge conflict at transplant time parks the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment), produces NO branch/PR, and re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head (existing #633 reset semantics).
- **AC5** — `po_accept` by a machine actor is refused (audit line only, no action); a second arm while a transplant is open is a no-op; the source PR closed by hand before the tick is skipped.
- **AC6** — review verdicts carry to the transplant PR (`ai_pr_reviewed`, `pr_approved`) iff the transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff, else the transplant runs label-free (fresh review+validation).
- **AC7** — branch `ai/guest-NNN` is deleted when the transplant PR reaches ANY closed state (merged or closed).

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-plan` — transplant plan computation: source eligibility (fork/draft/actor), branch name, verdict-carry diffing decision, park reason selection. → AC1, AC4…

blocks.text:
This is a big goal ticket: guest fork PRs become machine PRs via `po_accept` transplant. I need to implement:

1. **SM rule `guest-transplant`** — a JQL-based rule in `sm.json` (or via smAgent) that finds open, non-draft, `po_accept`-labeled, non-machine-authored, cross-repo PRs. limit 1 per tick.
2. **localAction `transplant_guest_pr`** — JS logic that:
  - Creates branch `ai/guest-NN` = API merge(main, headSHA recorded at arm time)
  - Opens machine PR `[guest #NN] <title>` with Co-authored-by trailer and body linking the source
  - Closes source PR + comment naming both SHAs
  - Caries review verdicts iff diff identical
  - Conflict 409 → park with `blocked` label + distinct-reason comment
  - Branch deleted before tick → park with no-ref reason
  - Machine-actor arm → refuse (audit only)
  - Double-arm → no-op
  - Closed source → skip
  - Branch GC when transplant PR closes
  - Security Gate phase before secret-consuming jobs (workflow job `needs:`)
3. **Security Gate** — ordered, mandatory, manifest-configurable ahead of ordinary validation.
4. Config: `guestTransplantLabel` in `.dmtools/config.js` / `customParams`; rule inert by default (enabled only where configured).

- `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` — SM rules
- `js/smAgent.js` — SM agent
- `js/common/` — helpers (scm.js, etc.)
- `js/unit-tests/` — tests
- Look for gh-113 guest merge lane, merge window logic, validate-fresh, merge-validated rules.

The best approach:
1. New module `js/common/guestTransplant.js` — the pure decision core:
  - `transplantPlan(source, ctx)` — computes the plan from the source PR state: eligibility (cross-repo, non-draft, label, actor), branch name `ai/guest-NN`, PR title `[guest #NN] <title>` (sanitized), body, Co-authored-by trailer, verdict-carry decision (diff identical), park reason selection.
  - Sanitization helpers: `sanitizeTitle` (length, no newline smuggling), `sanitizeCoAuthor` (author names → sanitized trailer).
  - Security gate manifest helpers: `gatePlan(manifest)` — the ordered job list; verify the `needs:` wiring — every secret-consuming job transitively needs the gate.
  - Idempotency/snapshot: orphan branch detection (E5), one live transplant per source.
  - Carrier of arm-time SHA: E1 — record the SHA at arm time. Where? The comment on the source PR could carry a marker with the head SHA. Actually the machine-added label po_accept fires no labeled event we can read later... Actually the plan says "transplant uses the SHA RECORDED AT ARM TIME". Since we can't know when the label was added from the tick itself (the tick reads the current head), we should record the head SHA at arm time via an audit comment/marker on the source PR when first observed. Hmm — but the SM tick sees the PR after the label exists; the "arm time" SHA = the head SHA at the first tick that observes the arm. So the tick posts (or reads) a marker comment recording the observed head SHA at first sighting; subsequent ticks use that recorded SHA (no TOCTOU even if force-pushed between ticks). That's implementable: on first sighting, the action writes a machine-parseable marker comment `<!-- guest-transplant:source=NN sha=... -->`; on later ticks it reads the marker and uses the recorded SHA. But simpler: do the transplant in the SAME tick as the first sighting (the tick observes the label, uses the current head SHA immediately). E1's force-push scenario is "between arm and tick" — since the tick reads the head SHA when it runs the transplant, the SHA used IS the tick-time SHA... The requirement says "uses the SHA RECORDED AT ARM TIME; the comment names both SHAs (no TOCTOU)".

  Hmm. Actually a two-phase approach: first sighting records the SHA in a marker comment (arm observation), then the transplant executes with that recorded SHA; if the head moved since the marker (force-push after first sighting), we still use the recorded SHA and name both in the comment (recorded vs current? or recorded transplant head vs merge result SHA?). AC1 says "the source PR closed with a transplant comment naming both SHAs" — the two SHAs are (a) the transplanted source head SHA and (b) the merge-result/transplant-branch SHA (or the machine PR's head). I'll interpret: comment names the source head SHA used and the resulting merge-commit SHA on `ai/guest-NN`.

A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). The park-reset rule operates on `validation_failed` labels. For the guest transplant, AC4 says: "parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment), produces NO branch/PR, and re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head (existing #633 reset semantics)".

Given the engine's 'blocked' = human-hold freeze (items with 'blocked' are invisible to EVERY rule), parking with the literal label 'blocked' would freeze the source from ALL rules including any reset lane. But the ticket explicitly says label `blocked`. Note the park rule's query for park-reset excludes 'blocked' (`notLabels: [..., 'blocked']`), and queryPrs filters 'blocked' pre-mutex — so a blocked-labeled source is fully frozen.

The AC4 re-arm "if a later human push changes the head" — for the transplant rule, the SOURCE PR is a fork PR; a human push to the fork branch moves the head. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

Resolution: the transplant park needs its OWN reset probe that runs regardless of the freeze. Options:
1. Give the park a different machine label (e.g. `guest_transplant_blocked`) — but the ticket explicitly says `blocked` label. Hmm, "park the source PR with label `blocked` + a distinct-reason comment naming the conflict" — AC4: "parks the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment)". I'll follow the ticket: label 'blocked'.
2. Reset owner: the guest-transplant rule handles parked-source reset in its action? Can't see blocked items in query.
3. A dedicated reset path in the localAction that scans... The localAction receives only matched items.

Option: make the reset a query-level opt-out — `query.unparkBlocked: true`? That touches queryPrs' blocked filters: currently TWO places filter blocked: pre-mutex `items = items.filter(...blocked...)` and in the matched filter. If q.allowBlockedItems === true, skip both filters. Then the guest-transplant rule query adds `allowBlockedItems: true` so it CAN see its parked sources, and the action/plan logic:
- item has 'blocked' + park marker records parked head sha ('parked-head: <sha>') + current head DIFFERS → remove 'blocked' (audit line), re-arm → the plan proceeds to transplant in the SAME tick? AC4: "re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head" — next tick would then transplant (or same tick — but limit 1 and the reset consumes the slot; keep it same-tick-simple: reset then continue to transplant in the same action? The action processes one ticket; after un-parking, it can proceed with the transplant immediately — fewer ticks, still serial).
- item has 'blocked' + head UNCHANGED vs parked sha → skip (still parked).
- item has 'blocked' + NO marker → skip (human hold — the machine never touches unknown blocked).

This is the gh-994 pattern transplanted into the guest lane: "when the park comment records the punished head sha ('parked-head: <sha>') and the current headRefOid DIFFERS, the label is removed UNCONDITIONALLY". I'll mirror exactly that marker format ('parked-head: <sha>') so the reset semantics are literally the "existing #633 reset semantics".

Hmm wait — do I really need `allowBlockedItems`? Consider: the parked source has 'blocked'. The transplant rule's query would need to see it. With allowBlockedItems the query sees it; the plan decides. This is a small, well-guarded opt-out documented as the gh-994 reset for the guest lane. The freeze invariant (fa #939) stays intact for all other rules because only this rule opts in, and its plan SKIPS blocked items whose head didn't change (or without our own marker). A human 'blocked' on a po_accept-labeled fork PR without our marker → skipped (respects human hold).

Wait, actually, there's a subtlety — the freeze exists so the machine doesn't touch human-frozen items. With allowBlockedItems, the transplant rule touches blocked items ONLY when (a) the item carries our transplant park marker AND (b) the head changed. That preserves the freeze semantics precisely.

The diff tools return unified diff text. So the carry decision can fingerprint the raw diff TEXT (byte-identical diff = identical diff text modulo the diff headers that differ by SHAs...). Careful: unified diff headers contain `index <sha>..<sha>` lines that differ between the source PR diff and the transplant PR diff even when the content is identical (different base/heads → different blob shas? Actually blob SHAs are content-based, so identical content → identical blob shas; but `--- a/... +++ b/...` and hunk headers are content-based too. The `index` line hashes blob contents — identical content gives identical blobs. The diff of the same changes against the same base main → byte-identical modulo nothing. But if main moved between review and transplant, the diff would differ → carry drops — which is CORECT (diff drifted).

Hmm — but the transplant branch is cut at CURRENT main; the reviewed source diff was against main-at-review-time. If main moved, the transplanted diff genuinely differs (merge resolution) → no carry. Byte-identical check is honest.

To be robust against headers: fingerprint = canonicalized diff text with `index` lines stripped and diff-range headers (`diff --git`, `index`) normalized away, keeping per-file paths + hunks. That's a pure function `diffFingerprint(diffText)`. For AC6 "iff the transplanted diff is byte-identical" — strict byte equality would break on index-line blob shas only when blob shas differ... blob shas are content-addressed; same final content → same blobs even if the base moved? No: blob sha = hash of FILE content (git blobs), independent of base. So identical file contents → identical index lines. Actually the `index abc..def 100644` — both sides hash the pre-image and post-image blobs. Pre-image = base file content. If main's file changed between review and transplant, pre-image differs → index differs → byte-diff → no carry. Correct semantics!

But wait — the diff produced for the SOURCE PR (against base at review time) vs TRANSPLANT PR (against current main): if main didn't move, byte-identical. If main moved, the diffs differ → no carry. Exactly the honest semantic. Keep a normalization that only strips NOTHING then — plain byte equality of the diff text? The diff text also carries the PR-specific headers? A unified diff from GitHub's .diff endpoint: starts with `diff --git a/x b/x`, index lines, etc. No PR metadata. One caveat: mode lines/rename detection should be stable too.

I'll implement `diffFingerprint(text)`: trim trailing whitespace per line? No — keep it strict: normalize line endings (\r\n → \n) and strip nothing else; return null for unusable (empty/null). "byte-identical" per ticket. Good — simple, honest, testable.

The diff tools return unified diff text. So the carry decision can fingerprint the raw diff TEXT (byte-identical diff = identical diff text modulo the diff headers that differ by SHAs...). Careful: unified diff headers contain `index <sha>..<sha>` lines that differ between the source PR diff and the transplant PR diff even when the content is identical (different base/heads → different blob shas? Actually blob SHAs are content-based, so identical content → identical blob shas; but `--- a/... +++ b/...` and hunk headers are content-based too. The `index` line hashes blob contents — identical content gives identical blobs. The diff of the same changes against the same base main → byte-identical modulo nothing. But if main moved between review and transplant, the diff would differ → carry drops — which is CORECT (diff drifted).

Hmm — but the transplant branch is cut at CURRENT main; the reviewed source diff was against main-at-review-time. If main moved, the transplanted diff genuinely differs (merge resolution) → no carry. Byte-identical check is honest.

To be robust against headers: fingerprint = canonicalized diff text with `index` lines stripped and diff-range headers (`diff --git`, `index`) normalized away, keeping per-file paths + hunks. That's a pure function `diffFingerprint(diffText)`. For AC6 "iff the transplanted diff is byte-identical" — strict byte equality would break on index-line blob shas only when blob shas differ... blob shas are content-addressed; same final content → same blobs even if the base moved? No: blob sha = hash of FILE content (git blobs), independent of base. So identical file contents → identical index lines. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

blocks.text:
The park-reset rule operates on `validation_failed` labels. For the guest transplant, AC4 says: "parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment), produces NO branch/PR, and re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head (existing #633 reset semantics)".

Given the engine's 'blocked' = human-hold freeze (items with 'blocked' are invisible to EVERY rule), parking with the literal label 'blocked' would freeze the source from ALL rules including any reset lane. But the ticket explicitly says label `blocked`. Note the park rule's query for park-reset excludes 'blocked' (`notLabels: [..., 'blocked']`), and queryPrs filters 'blocked' pre-mutex — so a blocked-labeled source is fully frozen.

The AC4 re-arm "if a later human push changes the head" — for the transplant rule, the SOURCE PR is a fork PR; a human push to the fork branch moves the head. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

Given the engine's 'blocked' = human-hold freeze (items with 'blocked' are invisible to EVERY rule), parking with the literal label 'blocked' would freeze the source from ALL rules including any reset lane. But the ticket explicitly says label `blocked`. Note the park rule's query for park-reset excludes 'blocked' (`notLabels: [..., 'blocked']`), and queryPrs filters 'blocked' pre-mutex — so a blocked-labeled source is fully frozen.

The AC4 re-arm "if a later human push changes the head" — for the transplant rule, the SOURCE PR is a fork PR; a human push to the fork branch moves the head. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

Resolution: the transplant park needs its OWN reset probe that runs regardless of the freeze. Options:
1. Give the park a different machine label (e.g. `guest_transplant_blocked`) — but the ticket explicitly says `blocked` label. Hmm, "park the source PR with label `blocked` + a distinct-reason comment naming the conflict" — AC4: "parks the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment)". I'll follow the ticket: label 'blocked'.

Option: make the reset a query-level opt-out — `query.unparkBlocked: true`? - item has 'blocked' + park marker records parked head sha ('parked-head: <sha>') + current head DIFFERS → remove 'blocked' (audit line), re-arm → the plan proceeds to transplant in the SAME tick? The park-reset rule operates on `validation_failed` labels. For the guest transplant, AC4 says: "parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment), produces NO branch/PR, and re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head (existing #633 reset semantics)".

Given the engine's 'blocked' = human-hold freeze (items with 'blocked' are invisible to EVERY rule), parking with the literal label 'blocked' would freeze the source from ALL rules including any reset lane. But the ticket explicitly says label `blocked`. Note the park rule's query for park-reset excludes 'blocked' (`notLabels: [..., 'blocked']`), and queryPrs filters 'blocked' pre-mutex — so a blocked-labeled source is fully frozen.

The AC4 re-arm "if a later human push changes the head" — for the transplant rule, the SOURCE PR is a fork PR; a human push to the fork branch moves the head. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

Resolution: the transplant park needs its OWN reset probe that runs regardless of the freeze. Options:
1. Give the park a different machine label (e.g. `guest_transplant_blocked`) — but the ticket explicitly says `blocked` label. Hmm, "park the source PR with label `blocked` + a distinct-reason comment naming the conflict" — AC4: "parks the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment)". I'll follow the ticket: label 'blocked'.
2. Reset owner: the guest-transplant rule handles parked-source reset in its action? Can't see blocked items in query.
3. A dedicated reset path in the localAction that scans... The localAction receives only matched items.

Option: make the reset a query-level opt-out — `query.unparkBlocked: true`? That touches queryPrs' blocked filters: currently TWO places filter blocked: pre-mutex `items = items.filter(...blocked...)` and in the matched filter. If q.allowBlockedItems === true, skip both filters. Then the guest-transplant rule query adds `allowBlockedItems: true` so it CAN see its parked sources, and the action/plan logic:
- item has 'blocked' + park marker records parked head sha ('parked-head: <sha>') + current head DIFFERS → remove 'blocked' (audit line), re-arm → the plan proceeds to transplant in the SAME tick? AC4: "re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head" — next tick would then transplant (or same tick — but limit 1 and the reset consumes the slot; keep it same-tick-simple: reset then continue to transplant in the same action? The action processes one ticket; after un-parking, it can proceed with the transplant immediately — fewer ticks, still serial).
- item has 'blocked' + head UNCHANGED vs parked sha → skip (still parked).

The diff tools return unified diff text. So the carry decision can fingerprint the raw diff TEXT (byte-identical diff = identical diff text modulo the diff headers that differ by SHAs...). Careful: unified diff headers contain `index <sha>..<sha>` lines that differ between the source PR diff and the transplant PR diff even when the content is identical (different base/heads → different blob shas? Actually blob SHAs are content-based, so identical content → identical blob shas; but `--- a/... +++ b/...` and hunk headers are content-based too. The `index` line hashes blob contents — identical content gives identical blobs. The diff of the same changes against the same base main → byte-identical modulo nothing. But if main moved between review and transplant, the diff would differ → carry drops — which is CORECT (diff drifted).

Hmm — but the transplant branch is cut at CURRENT main; the reviewed source diff was against main-at-review-time. If main moved, the transplanted diff genuinely differs (merge resolution) → no carry. Byte-identical check is honest.

To be robust against headers: fingerprint = canonicalized diff text with `index` lines stripped and diff-range headers (`diff --git`, `index`) normalized away, keeping per-file paths + hunks. That's a pure function `diffFingerprint(diffText)`. For AC6 "iff the transplanted diff is byte-identical" — strict byte equality would break on index-line blob shas only when blob shas differ... blob shas are content-addressed; same final content → same blobs even if the base moved? No: blob sha = hash of FILE content (git blobs), independent of base. So identical file contents → identical index lines. Actually the `index abc..def 100644` — both sides hash the pre-image and post-image blobs. Pre-image = base file content. If main's file changed between review and transplant, pre-image differs → index differs → byte-diff → no carry. Correct semantics!

But wait — the diff produced for the SOURCE PR (against base at review time) vs TRANSPLANT PR (against current main): if main didn't move, byte-identical. If main moved, the diffs differ → no carry. Exactly the honest semantic. Keep a normalization that only strips NOTHING then — plain byte equality of the diff text? The diff text also carries the PR-specific headers? A unified diff from GitHub's .diff endpoint: starts with `diff --git a/x b/x`, index lines, etc. No PR metadata. One caveat: mode lines/rename detection should be stable too.

I'll implement `diffFingerprint(text)`: trim trailing whitespace per line? No — keep it strict: normalize line endings (\r\n → \n) and strip nothing else; return null for unusable (empty/null). "byte-identical" per ticket. Good — simple, honest, testable.

blocks.text:
The park-reset rule operates on `validation_failed` labels. For the guest transplant, AC4 says: "parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment), produces NO branch/PR, and re-arms automatically if a later human push changes the head (existing #633 reset semantics)".

Given the engine's 'blocked' = human-hold freeze (items with 'blocked' are invisible to EVERY rule), parking with the literal label 'blocked' would freeze the source from ALL rules including any reset lane. But the ticket explicitly says label `blocked`. Note the park rule's query for park-reset excludes 'blocked' (`notLabels: [..., 'blocked']`), and queryPrs filters 'blocked' pre-mutex — so a blocked-labeled source is fully frozen.

The AC4 re-arm "if a later human push changes the head" — for the transplant rule, the SOURCE PR is a fork PR; a human push to the fork branch moves the head. The reset must UN-park (remove 'blocked') and let the next tick transplant. Since the 'blocked' freeze is engine-wide, the transplant rule itself cannot see the parked source.

Resolution: the transplant park needs its OWN reset probe that runs regardless of the freeze. Options:
1. Give the park a different machine label (e.g. `guest_transplant_blocked`) — but the ticket explicitly says `blocked` label. The diff tools return unified diff text. So the carry decision can fingerprint the raw diff TEXT (byte-identical diff = identical diff text modulo the diff headers that differ by SHAs...). Careful: unified diff headers contain `index <sha>..<sha>` lines that differ between the source PR diff and the transplant PR diff even when the content is identical (different base/heads → different blob shas? Actually blob SHAs are content-based, so identical content → identical blob shas; but `--- a/... +++ b/...` and hunk headers are content-based too. The `index` line hashes blob contents — identical content gives identical blobs. The diff of the same changes against the same base main → byte-identical modulo nothing. But if main moved between review and transplant, the diff would differ → carry drops — which is CORECT (diff drifted).

Hmm — but the transplant branch is cut at CURRENT main; the reviewed source diff was against main-at-review-time. If main moved, the transplanted diff genuinely differs (merge resolution) → no carry. Byte-identical check is honest.

To be robust against headers: fingerprint = canonicalized diff text with `index` lines stripped and diff-range headers (`diff --git`, `index`) normalized away, keeping per-file paths + hunks. That's a pure function `diffFingerprint(diffText)`. For AC6 "iff the transplanted diff is byte-identical" — strict byte equality would break on index-line blob shas only when blob shas differ... blob shas are content-addressed; same final content → same blobs even if the base moved? No: blob sha = hash of FILE content (git blobs), independent of base. So identical file contents → identical index lines. Actually the `index abc..def 100644` — both sides hash the pre-image and post-image blobs. Pre-image = base file content. If main's file changed between review and transplant, pre-image differs → index differs → byte-diff → no carry. Correct semantics!

But wait — the diff produced for the SOURCE PR (against base at review time) vs TRANSPLANT PR (against current main): if main didn't move, byte-identical. If main moved, the diffs differ → no carry. Exactly the honest semantic. Keep a normalization that only strips NOTHING then — plain byte equality of the diff text? The diff text also carries the PR-specific headers? A unified diff from GitHub's .diff endpoint: starts with `diff --git a/x b/x`, index lines, etc. No PR metadata. One caveat: mode lines/rename detection should be stable too.

I'll implement `diffFingerprint(text)`: trim trailing whitespace per line? No — keep it strict: normalize line endings (\r\n → \n) and strip nothing else; return null for unusable (empty/null). "byte-identical" per ticket. Good — simple, honest, testable.

- `q.allowBlockedItems: true` → skips the pre-mutex filter and the matched filter for this rule.

var allowBlocked = q.allowBlockedItems === true;
items = items.filter(function (it) { return allowBlocked || it.labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1; });
``
and in matched filter:
```js
if (!allowBlocked2 && labels.indexOf('blocked') !== -1) return false;

import json

    "id": "guest-transplant",
    "source": "github",
    "guestTransplant": True,
    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
path = 'sm_github.json'
d = json.load(open(path))
rules = d['params']['jobParams']['rules']
idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rules) if r.get('id') == 'conflict-rework')
new_rule = {
    "id": "guest-transplant",
    "source": "github",
    "guestTransplant": True,
    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "

        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

Wait — there's an issue: the `crossRepo` guard needs `item.headRepo`, which is set by `_prItemFromPr` in queryPrs (PR-carier items). But there's a subtlety: the guest-transplant rule's query would not trigger prStatus enrichment (`_prStatusFetchNeeded` doesn't include crossRepo — good, no extra API calls), and `item.headRepo` comes free from the list payload.

But also — the pre-query 'blocked' filter: AC4 requires the transplant rule to SEE parked (blocked) sources for the head-change reset. Currently queryPrs filters blocked items pre-mutex AND in the matched filter. I need an opt-out. Options:
- `q.allowBlockedItems: true` → skips the pre-mutex filter and the matched filter for this rule.

This modifies shared code minimally. The freeze invariant stays: only rules that explicitly opt in can see blocked items, and the guest-transplant decision core still refuses to act on a human 'blocked' (no marker) — tested.

```js
var allowBlocked = q.allowBlockedItems === true;
items = items.filter(function (it) { return allowBlocked || it.labels.indexOf('blocked') === -1; });
``
and in matched filter:
```js
if (!allowBlocked2 && labels.indexOf('blocked') !== -1) return false;
``
The matched filter uses q2 = rule.query; I'll compute allowBlocked there from q2.

Hmm — wait. Do I want to route the park-reset through the main rule? Reconsider: is it acceptable to keep AC4's re-arm handled WITHOUT seeing blocked items? Alternative: silent-update-behind (L1) operates on BEHIND PRs and would un-park... no, it updates branches, doesn't remove 'blocked'. park-reset handles validation_failed only. So yes, the transplant rule must see its own parked sources → allowBlockedItems opt-out it is.

    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "

        "notMachine": True,

}

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
path = 'sm_github.json'
d = json.load(open(path))
rules = d['params']['jobParams']['rules']
idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rules) if r.get('id') == 'conflict-rework')
new_rule = {
    "id": "guest-transplant",
    "source": "github",
    "guestTransplant": True,
    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
path = 'sm_github.json'
d = json.load(open(path))
rules = d['params']['jobParams']['rules']
idx = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rules) if r.get('id') == 'conflict-rework')
new_rule = {
    "id": "guest-transplant",
    "source": "github",
    "guestTransplant": True,
    "description": (
        "GUEST TRANSPLANT (gh-1140, supersedes the #1139 fix direction): a third-party fork PR labeled "
        "po_accept by a HUMAN (write-capable, non-machine — the labeled event is the voucher, machine "
        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "

        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "

        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "
        "the API merges endpoint (a fork head SHA is addressable in the base — no clone, no fork-owned ref "
        "is EVER targeted, no workflow_dispatch on a fork branch, no check run stamped on a fork head — "
        "impossible by construction), then the machine PR '[guest #N] <title>' opens with a Co-authored-by "
        "trailer and a body linking the source, review verdicts (ai_pr_reviewed, pr_approved) carry IFF the "
        "transplanted diff is byte-identical to the reviewed source diff (AC6 — anything else runs a fresh "
        "pipeline), and the source closes with a transplant comment naming both SHAs. From there the PR is "
        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "
        "DEFAULT (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures smGuestTransplant "
        "({label: 'po_accept', parkedLabel: 'blocked', branchPrefix: 'ai/guest-', baseBranch: 'main', "
        "carryLabels: [...], gate: {gateJobs: [...], secretJobs: [...]}}); the gh-113 manual-arm lane is "
        "untouched. limit 1 per tick — a transplant creates a PR and closes another, serial by construction "
        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),
    "query": {
        "type": "pr",
        "labels": ["po_accept"],
        "notLabels": ["agent:rework"],
        "notMachine": True,
        "crossRepo": True,
        "draft": False,
        "allowBlockedItems": True
    },
    "localAction": "transplant_guest_pr",
    "limit": 1
}
rules.insert(idx, new_rule)
json.dump(d, open(path, 'w'), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
open(path, 'a').write('\n')
print('inserted at', idx, '- rules now:', len(rules))
EOF"}

        "actors and proof-less arms refuse) is transplanted into an ordinary machine PR of the base repo: "
        "branch ai/guest-<N> is cut at main via the git refs API and the source head SHA merges in through "

        "indistinguishable from any same-repo machine PR: validate-fresh dispatches on the ai/guest-<N> "
        "branch, merge-validated merges it, zero guest-specific merge logic (AC2). SECURITY GATE (AC3): the "
        "repo's gate manifest (smGuestTransplant.gate) names the secret-free security jobs that must "
        "conclude green BEFORE any secret-consuming validation job — the ordering is enforced structurally "
        "in the target workflow's job graph (needs:) and asserted structurally by the gate wiring check "
        "(UT-gate); guest-ness is a ROUTING hint for the Gate, never a permanent mode. PARKS (AC4): a merges "
        "409 parks the source (blocked + distinct-reason comment) and produces NO branch/PR; a deleted/"
        "unreadable source head parks with the no-ref reason; both carry the 'parked-head: <sha>' marker so "
        "the #633 reset semantics re-arm automatically when a human push changes the head. SNAPSHOT "
        "SEMANTICS (AC5/E1/E5): the arm marker records the head SHA at arm time — a force-push between arm "
        "and tick transplants the RECORDED sha (no TOCTOU); a second arm while a transplant is open is a "
        "no-op; an orphan branch from a dead tick completes from its marker or is GC'd; the same tick's GC "
        "sweep deletes every ai/guest-* branch whose transplant PR reached ANY closed state (AC7). INERT BY "

        "(the merge-window discipline)."
    ),

        "notMachine": True,

}

EOF"}

`verdictMachineLogins` returns an array of logins (machineAuthorLogins output). My `classifyArmActor` handles arrays. When machineAuthor is unconfigured → empty array → classifyArmActor treats every actor as 'human' (machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(empty) → [] → return 'human'). Hmm — for AC5 ("po_accept by a machine actor is refused"), an unconfigured machineAuthor means we can't identify machine actors... The gh-828 doctrine: "an empty list trusts nothing" in some contexts. For the arm gate: no configured machine logins → a machine actor (e.g., the ai-bot) labeling po_accept would be treated as human → BAD? But without the knob the deployment has no machine identity at all — the guestValidationPath precedent: "No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all)" — isManualArm returns TRUE (external/human) when no logins configured. My choice mirrors the gh-113 precedent exactly. Consistent — keep.

3. The `mcpParse(github_list_prs(...))` in guestOpenPrOnBranch — fine.

4. In the engine, tickets from queryPrs have `title`? Yes — `_prItemFromPr` sets title, author, headRepo, draft. Good.

But the dry flag inside guestRunSteps is passed as the `dry` arg — good; but inside guestApplyStep the merge dry-run returns {mergedSha: s.headSha} → ctx.mergedSha set. open_pr dry → newPrNumber null — `out.newPrNumber !== undefined` → ctx.newPrNumber = null. OK.

6. IMPORTANT — processRule's early return for inert rule: I return `{ processedKeys: [], skippedKeys: [] }`. Fine.

7. `rule.query.labels = [guestCfg.label]` — the engine logs the query AFTER my patch? The query log line ("Query[github]: ...") is printed BEFORE my patch? Order in processRule: label log + query log happens right after interpolatedJql (~line 1710), and the enabled check at 1717 — my patch is AFTER the query log print (the tickets block starts after the enabled check at ~1720). So the log shows the pre-patch label 'po_accept'... The patch happens before source.query — behavior correct; only the log line shows the JSON default. Acceptable (could confuse debug). Move the log? The query log happens before `rule.enabled` check; I can't easily print post-patch without moving code. Fine — the JSON in the file documents the default spelling; the tick's actual query uses the configured label. Minor.

8. GralJS strictness: `String.prototype.replace` with regex + function — fine. `Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter/some` — fine. Template literals — none. Arrow functions — let me double check my smAgent additions... I used `function (n) { return n.trim(); }` etc. — fine. My guard functions (matchesGuards with guestTransplantModule) run on the MAIN engine only — queryPrs runs main-engine. But hold on: `ISSUE_SEARCH_WORKER_SOURCE` and `PR_STATUS_WORKER_SOURCE` run via smAsync on fresh engines — they don't call matchesGuards. Correct.

12. One more risk: `dmtools compile` pack closure — smAgent.js now requires guestTransplant.js (file-relative, load-time) — discovered. guestTransplant requires machineAuthor (already in closure). Good.

And validate-fresh dispatches on the branch — the ai/guest-42 branch EXISTS in the base repo (created by us) → workflow_dispatch works. That's the whole point of the transplant. AC2 satisfied structurally — no new merge logic.

Also the silent-update-behind / park rules may touch the guest PR branch — they operate on the ai/guest-42 branch in the base — fine, machine-owned.

E4: rework legs on the transplant PR — machine rules fix the branch; the closed source is never reopened (nothing in my code reopens PRs). Good.

`verdictMachineLogins` returns an array of logins (machineAuthorLogins output). My `classifyArmActor` handles arrays. The gh-828 doctrine: "an empty list trusts nothing" in some contexts. For the arm gate: no configured machine logins → a machine actor (e.g., the ai-bot) labeling po_accept would be treated as human → BAD? But without the knob the deployment has no machine identity at all — the guestValidationPath precedent: "No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all)" — isManualArm returns TRUE (external/human) when no logins configured. My choice mirrors the gh-113 precedent exactly. Consistent — keep.

3. The `mcpParse(github_list_prs(...))` in guestOpenPrOnBranch — fine.

4. In the engine, tickets from queryPrs have `title`? Yes — `_prItemFromPr` sets title, author, headRepo, draft. Good.

5. The dry-run path in transplantGuestPrAction: dry + decision transplant → guestRunSteps(..., dry=true). But the dry flag inside guestRunSteps is passed as the `dry` arg — good; but inside guestApplyStep the merge dry-run returns {mergedSha: s.headSha} → ctx.mergedSha set. open_pr dry → newPrNumber null — `out.newPrNumber !== undefined` → ctx.newPrNumber = null. OK.

So the log shows the pre-patch label 'po_accept'... The patch happens before source.query — behavior correct; only the log line shows the JSON default. Acceptable (could confuse debug). Move the log? The query log happens before `rule.enabled` check; I can't easily print post-patch without moving code. Fine — the JSON in the file documents the default spelling; the tick's actual query uses the configured label. Minor.

8. GralJS strictness: `String.prototype.replace` with regex + function — fine. `Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter/some` — fine. Template literals — none. Arrow functions — let me double check my smAgent additions... I used `function (n) { return n.trim(); }` etc. — fine. 9. `checkRunStampModule.tempBodyPath` no longer used in my code (removed) — good.

But hold on: `ISSUE_SEARCH_WORKER_SOURCE` and `PR_STATUS_WORKER_SOURCE` run via smAsync on fresh engines — they don't call matchesGuards. Correct.

12. One more risk: `dmtools compile` pack closure — smAgent.js now requires guestTransplant.js (file-relative, load-time) — discovered. guestTransplant requires machineAuthor (already in closure). Good.

Now, the ticket's AC2/IT-lanes: transplanted PR walks validate-fresh → merge-validated with zero guest-lane invocations. AC2 satisfied structurally — no new merge logic.

Also the silent-update-behind / park rules may touch the guest PR branch — they operate on the ai/guest-42 branch in the base — fine, machine-owned.

blocks.text:
`verdictMachineLogins` returns an array of logins (machineAuthorLogins output). My `classifyArmActor` handles arrays. When machineAuthor is unconfigured → empty array → classifyArmActor treats every actor as 'human' (machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(empty) → [] → return 'human'). Hmm — for AC5 ("po_accept by a machine actor is refused"), an unconfigured machineAuthor means we can't identify machine actors... The gh-828 doctrine: "an empty list trusts nothing" in some contexts. For the arm gate: no configured machine logins → a machine actor (e.g., the ai-bot) labeling po_accept would be treated as human → BAD? But without the knob the deployment has no machine identity at all — the guestValidationPath precedent: "No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all)" — isManualArm returns TRUE (external/human) when no logins configured. My choice mirrors the gh-113 precedent exactly. Consistent — keep.

3. The `mcpParse(github_list_prs(...))` in guestOpenPrOnBranch — fine.

4. In the engine, tickets from queryPrs have `title`? Yes — `_prItemFromPr` sets title, author, headRepo, draft. Good.

5. The dry-run path in transplantGuestPrAction: dry + decision transplant → guestRunSteps(..., dry=true). But the dry flag inside guestRunSteps is passed as the `dry` arg — good; but inside guestApplyStep the merge dry-run returns {mergedSha: s.headSha} → ctx.mergedSha set. open_pr dry → newPrNumber null — `out.newPrNumber !== undefined` → ctx.newPrNumber = null. OK.

6. IMPORTANT — processRule's early return for inert rule: I return `{ processedKeys: [], skippedKeys: [] }`. Fine.

7. `rule.query.labels = [guestCfg.label]` — the engine logs the query AFTER my patch? The query log line ("Query[github]: ...") is printed BEFORE my patch? Order in processRule: label log + query log happens right after interpolatedJql (~line 1710), and the enabled check at 1717 — my patch is AFTER the query log print (the tickets block starts after the enabled check at ~1720). So the log shows the pre-patch label 'po_accept'... The patch happens before source.query — behavior correct; only the log line shows the JSON default. Acceptable (could confuse debug). Move the log? The query log happens before `rule.enabled` check; I can't easily print post-patch without moving code. Fine — the JSON in the file documents the default spelling; the tick's actual query uses the configured label. Minor.

8. GralJS strictness: `String.prototype.replace` with regex + function — fine. `Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter/some` — fine. Template literals — none. Arrow functions — let me double check my smAgent additions... I used `function (n) { return n.trim(); }` etc. — fine. In guestTransplant.js: no arrows — I wrote `jobs.forEach(function (j) {...})` — fine. One risk: in `gateOrderedIds` I have a comment `// eslint-disable-next-line no-param-reassign` — harmless.

9. `checkRunStampModule.tempBodyPath` no longer used in my code (removed) — good.

10. sm_github.json description has literal newlines? No — single line string in JSON. Python wrote it as one long line. Good.

11. The pack-require path pin: `test_packRequirePath.js` scans for deferred requires. My requires are top-level. But note githubSource.js is part of the pack — its `require('../../common/guestTransplant.js')` at load time — fine.

Wait — one important detail: worker sources in githubSource execute on fresh engines with `require('./common/smProvider.js')` — worker requires are js-root-relative. My guard functions (matchesGuards with guestTransplantModule) run on the MAIN engine only — queryPrs runs main-engine. But hold on: `ISSUE_SEARCH_WORKER_SOURCE` and `PR_STATUS_WORKER_SOURCE` run via smAsync on fresh engines — they don't call matchesGuards. Correct.

12. One more risk: `dmtools compile` pack closure — smAgent.js now requires guestTransplant.js (file-relative, load-time) — discovered. guestTransplant requires machineAuthor (already in closure). Good.

Now, the ticket's AC2/IT-lanes: transplanted PR walks validate-fresh → merge-validated with zero guest-lane invocations. Check merge-validated-guest (gh-113 lane) doesn't fire on the transplanted PR: that rule matches `notMachine: true` (guest = non-machine-authored) — the transplant PR is MACHINE-authored → the gh-113 guest lane can never match it (it fires merge_pr via guestZeroFailing on NON-machine PRs only). And validate-fresh dispatches on the branch — the ai/guest-42 branch EXISTS in the base repo (created by us) → workflow_dispatch works. That's the whole point of the transplant. AC2 satisfied structurally — no new merge logic.

Also the silent-update-behind / park rules may touch the guest PR branch — they operate on the ai/guest-42 branch in the base — fine, machine-owned.

E4: rework legs on the transplant PR — machine rules fix the branch; the closed source is never reopened (nothing in my code reopens PRs). Good.

Now wait for the full suite. Meanwhile, let me write outputs/response.md draft content per output_rules (concise PR description). But FIRST verify the full suite passes. Let me poll the job.

`verdictMachineLogins` returns an array of logins (machineAuthorLogins output). My `classifyArmActor` handles arrays.
