The gh-828 doctrine: "an empty list trusts nothing" in some contexts. For the arm gate: no configured machine logins → a machine actor (e.g., the ai-bot) labeling po_accept would be treated as human → BAD? But without the knob the deployment has no machine identity at all — the guestValidationPath precedent: "No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all)" — isManualArm returns TRUE (external/human) when no logins configured. My choice mirrors the gh-113 precedent exactly. Consistent — keep.

3. The `mcpParse(github_list_prs(...))` in guestOpenPrOnBranch — fine.

4. In the engine, tickets from queryPrs have `title`? Yes — `_prItemFromPr` sets title, author, headRepo, draft. Good.

5. The dry-run path in transplantGuestPrAction: dry + decision transplant → guestRunSteps(..., dry=true). But the dry flag inside guestRunSteps is passed as the `dry` arg — good; but inside guestApplyStep the merge dry-run returns {mergedSha: s.headSha} → ctx.mergedSha set. open_pr dry → newPrNumber null — `out.newPrNumber !== undefined` → ctx.newPrNumber = null. OK.

So the log shows the pre-patch label 'po_accept'... The patch happens before source.query — behavior correct; only the log line shows the JSON default. Acceptable (could confuse debug). Move the log? The query log happens before `rule.enabled` check; I can't easily print post-patch without moving code. Fine — the JSON in the file documents the default spelling; the tick's actual query uses the configured label. Minor.

8. GralJS strictness: `String.prototype.replace` with regex + function — fine. `Array.prototype.forEach/map/filter/some` — fine. Template literals — none. Arrow functions — let me double check my smAgent additions... I used `function (n) { return n.trim(); }` etc. — fine. 9. `checkRunStampModule.tempBodyPath` no longer used in my code (removed) — good.

But hold on: `ISSUE_SEARCH_WORKER_SOURCE` and `PR_STATUS_WORKER_SOURCE` run via smAsync on fresh engines — they don't call matchesGuards. Correct.

12. One more risk: `dmtools compile` pack closure — smAgent.js now requires guestTransplant.js (file-relative, load-time) — discovered. guestTransplant requires machineAuthor (already in closure). Good.

Now, the ticket's AC2/IT-lanes: transplanted PR walks validate-fresh → merge-validated with zero guest-lane invocations. AC2 satisfied structurally — no new merge logic.

Also the silent-update-behind / park rules may touch the guest PR branch — they operate on the ai/guest-42 branch in the base — fine, machine-owned.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  L[po_accept by a human] --> R[rule guest-transplant: transplantSequence]
  R -->|machine/proof-less actor| X[refuse - audit only]
  R -->|conflict 409 / no-ref| P[park blocked + parked-head marker - #633 re-arm]
  R -->|eligible| B[refs API: ai/guest-N at main]
  B --> M[merges API: recorded source SHA]
  M --> PR[machine PR guest #N + Co-authored-by + carry iff identical diff]
  PR --> G[Security Gate jobs first - needs: wiring asserted]
  G --> V[validate-fresh then merge-validated - standard lanes]
  V --> GC[PR closed/merged - branch GC deletes ai/guest-N]
</details>
","path":"outputs/response.md"}
```

`verdictMachineLogins` returns an array of logins (machineAuthorLogins output). My `classifyArmActor` handles arrays. When machineAuthor is unconfigured → empty array → classifyArmActor treats every actor as 'human' (machineAuthorModule.machineAuthorLogins(empty) → [] → return 'human'). Hmm — for AC5 ("po_accept by a machine actor is refused"), an unconfigured machineAuthor means we can't identify machine actors... The gh-828 doctrine: "an empty list trusts nothing" in some contexts. For the arm gate: no configured machine logins → a machine actor (e.g., the ai-bot) labeling po_accept would be treated as human → BAD? But without the knob the deployment has no machine identity at all — the guestValidationPath precedent: "No machineAuthor configured → every actor is external (a deployment without the knob has no machine identity at all)" — isManualArm returns TRUE (external/human) when no logins configured. My choice mirrors the gh-113 precedent exactly. Consistent — keep.

{"content":"### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

{"content":"### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

{"content":"### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). - One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.

content.text:
### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.

{"content":"### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). ### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.

### What changed
Guest fork PRs labeled `po_accept` (by a human) are transplanted by the SM into ordinary machine PRs: branch `ai/guest-<N>` cut at main via the refs API, the recorded source head SHA merged in via the API merges endpoint, machine PR `[guest #N] <title>` opened with a Co-authored-by trailer + source link, source closed with a comment naming both SHAs, verdicts carried iff the diff is byte-identical — then the PR walks the standard validate-fresh → merge-validated lanes with zero fork-specific code (AC1/AC2/AC6). Merge conflicts and deleted heads park the source (`blocked` + distinct-reason comment carrying the `parked-head:` marker for the existing #633 auto re-arm); branch GC deletes `ai/guest-*` when the transplant PR reaches any closed state (AC4/AC7).

### Key decisions
- One SM rule (`guest-transplant`, `localAction: transplant_guest_pr`, limit 1/tick) + one pure decision core (`js/common/guestTransplant.js`, UT-plan/UT-gate): the wiring only probes state and executes the returned steps — refusals (machine/proof-less actor), double-arm no-ops, human holds, arm-time-SHA pinning (E1) and orphan-branch recovery (E5) are all pure, unit-tested decisions.
- Inert by default (REG-guest113): the rule fires only where the project configures `smGuestTransplant` (label, parked label, branch prefix, carry labels, gate manifest) — the gh-113 manual-arm lane is untouched.
- Security Gate is structural (AC3): `validateGateWiring` refuses any job graph where a secret-consuming job does not transitively `needs:` a gate job; the serialized dispatch plan orders every gate job ahead of every secret job. No fork-owned ref is ever targeted — the transport addresses only the base repo and the machine-owned `ai/guest-<N>` branch.
- New query guards in `githubSource.js`: `crossRepo` (fail-closed on same-repo/deleted-fork heads) and `allowBlockedItems` (opt-in so the AC4 park-reset lane can see its own parked sources; the fa#939 freeze holds everywhere else).

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_guestTransplant.json   # 52 tests (AC1..AC7, E1/E3/E5, UT-gate)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json               # 5594 passed, 0 failed (REG-samerepo)
```

The IT-transplant/IT-lanes/E2E-scratch legs (fake/live GitHub) stay environment-bound — their decision cores (plan, sequence, gate wiring, GC) are the UT-covered pure module; the transport is byte-pinned command builders.
